title: The 5 Animals That Survive the Deepest Cold, Ranked (#1 Is Tiny)

scenes.text: Polar bears don't make this list. Number one is barely visible to your eye.
Number five: the Arctic ground squirrel. Its body drops to minus three degrees Celsius while it hibernates.
scenes.label: Arctic ground squirrel · -3°C

scenes.text: Number four: the Alaska wood frog. Frozen solid at minus eighteen, for up to seven months.
scenes.label: Wood frog · -18°C

scenes.text: Number three: the Arctic woolly bear caterpillar. It freezes solid at minus fifty, winter after winter.
scenes.label: Woolly bear · -50°C

scenes.text: Number two: the red flat bark beetle larva. In lab tests, its insides turned to glass and it survived minus one hundred.
scenes.label: Bark beetle larva · -100°C

scenes.text: Number one: the tardigrade, about half a millimeter long. It has survived minus two hundred degrees.
scenes.label: Tardigrade · -200°C

description:
The five animals known to survive the lowest temperatures: the Arctic ground squirrel (body at minus 2.9 C in hibernation), the Alaska wood frog (frozen at minus 18 C for up to 218 days), the Arctic woolly bear caterpillar (frozen solid at minus 50 C or below), the red flat bark beetle larva (vitrified, survived minus 100 C in lab tests and reportedly down to minus 150 C) and the tardigrade (minus 200 C in the lab).
Which one surprised you most?
